title: Decoder bridge: adaptive token synchronizer and KV flush reorder to reduce prefill tail latency
author: Nina Patel
description: Motivation: Small but frequent multi-stream prefill workloads show long tail latency when prefill KV commit/flush serializes decode start for a subset of shards. This PR introduces a lightweight 'decoder bridge' microkernel and an adaptive token synchronizer that allow decode work to start opportunistically while guaranteeing KV coherence; additionally we reorder background KV flush/writeback to prioritize in-flight slices to reduce stall probability. Design summary: 1) decoder_bridge microkernel exposes a narrow ABI that accepts partial prefill completion tokens and a safe continuation point for decode kernels so that decode can start for slices whose KV is ready while the rest of the prefill continues in background; 2) token_synchronizer tracks per-request slice readiness and uses an adaptive threshold (configurable percentile + min-slices) to decide early decode handoff; 3) kv_flush_reorderer introduces a prioritized writeback queue that promotes writes for slices with active decode handoffs and demotes cold writebacks; 4) integration with the scheduler: small change to Scheduler::sliceApply to publish readiness events to the synchronizer; 5) safety: full correctness ensured by a KV pin + read-after-write validation step in the bridge kernel before final decode commit. Checklist: implementation and unit tests implemented; perf harness and synthetic multi-stream tests added; runtime flags for toggling feature and tuning thresholds; documentation update and migration notes added. Testing: local microbenchmarks across 4 GPU shapes, cluster perf runs on staging with mixed small/large request mixes; canary rollout planned. Benchmarks: on mixed-small workload (mean 6 tokens prefill, 120 concurrent streams) P95 latency reduced ~12% and 99th reduced ~18% compared to baseline; end-to-end token cost unchanged within noise. Backward compatibility: feature gated and off by default; non-breaking by default. Rollback plan: revert feature flag or disable via console; migration safe because no on-disk state changes. Related work: ENG-1442 (prefill scheduling work), PRs: pr-82763, pr-89901 for context. Merge method: squash. Notes: avoided major changes to KV store internals; kept kernel ABI minimal to ease backporting to release branches.
